description: Table 7 is a single rendered data table (6 data rows x 6 columns) reporting average grain size (AGS) and dynamic-recrystallisation grain (DRXG) volume fractions for a low-alloy steel deformed to 0.9 strain under constant conditions and under transiently decreasing Z_P. Column headers as printed: "Deformation conditions", "AGS of DRXGsI (μm)", "Volume fraction of DRXGsI", "AGS of DRXGsII (μm)", "Volume fraction of DRXGsII", "AGS of final microstructure (μm)". Two baseline rows, "950 °C, 0.01 s−1" and "1050 °C, 0.01 s−1", carry em dashes in all four DRXG columns (no DRX grains recorded) with final AGS of 52.52 and 79.89 μm. Four transient rows pair each baseline with a step change at 0.2 or 0.4 strain: "950 °C, 0.1–0.01 s−1" and "950–1050 °C, 0.01 s−1". In both, AGS of DRXGsI rises with the strain at which the change occurs (34.82 → 46.11 μm; 43.57 → 61.89 μm) as does its volume fraction (0.02 → 0.24; 0.01 → 0.13), while DRXGsII retains the dominant volume fraction (0.97/0.76 and 0.99/0.86). Final AGS is essentially unchanged at 950 °C (52.10–52.58 μm) and is slightly refined by the temperature step (78.50, 75.90 μm vs 79.89 μm), i.e. a transient Z_P decrease barely moves the final grain size away from the constant-condition value.

subfigures.description: Single rendered table with six rows and six columns: deformation conditions and five numeric quantities (AGS of DRXGsI in μm, volume fraction of DRXGsI, AGS of DRXGsII in μm, volume fraction of DRXGsII, AGS of final microstructure in μm). Two constant-condition rows contain em dashes in all DRXG columns; four transient rows contain full numeric values. No images, plots, scale bars or colour scales are present.

observations.observation: Constant-condition rows '950 °C, 0.01 s−1' and '1050 °C, 0.01 s−1' contain em dashes (—) for both AGS of DRXGsI/DRXGsII and both volume fractions, with AGS of final microstructure equal to 52.52 μm and 79.89 μm respectively.
For '950 °C, 0.1–0.01 s−1', AGS of DRXGsI increases from 34.82 μm at 0.2 strain to 46.11 μm at 0.4 strain, and its volume fraction increases from 0.02 to 0.24.
For '950–1050 °C, 0.01 s−1', AGS of DRXGsI increases from 43.57 μm at 0.2 strain to 61.89 μm at 0.4 strain, and its volume fraction increases from 0.01 to 0.13.
DRXGsII holds the dominant volume fraction in all four transient rows: 0.97 and 0.76 for the 950 °C rows, 0.99 and 0.86 for the 950–1050 °C rows.
AGS of DRXGsII is 52.57 μm and 54.32 μm for the 950 °C transient rows, and 78.62 μm and 77.83 μm for the 950–1050 °C transient rows.

AGS of the final microstructure is nearly identical for all three 950 °C conditions (52.52 μm constant, 52.10 μm at 0.2 strain, 52.58 μm at 0.4 strain) despite the presence of DRX grains in the two transient cases.
The final microstructure is refined by the transient temperature increase: 79.89 μm (constant 1050 °C, 0.01 s−1) versus 78.50 μm (0.2 strain) and 75.90 μm (0.4 strain) for 950–1050 °C, 0.01 s−1.
The caption states that Table 7 presents AGS evolutions at 0.9 strain under constant conditions and decreasing Z_P.

The citing text states that, unlike the results under suddenly increasing Z_P, there was no obvious difference in the final grain size after transiently decreasing Z_P between experiment and simulation.
The citing text states that compared to the increasing-Z_P simulation results in Table 6, the remaining volume fraction of DRXGs in Table 7 was significantly lower, especially when ε1 was 0.4.
The citing text states that DRXGsI could grow rapidly to a size nearly identical to that observed under the corresponding constant condition after an instantaneous decrease in Z_P.

The citing text states that DRXGsII nucleated and grew quickly after the transient Z_P decrease and that the AGS of DRXGsII soon surpassed that of DRXGsI, reaching the level of the corresponding constant condition (Fig. 27c and 27d).

measured_quantities: strain at which the transient condition change occurs (0.2, 0.4)
unreadable_items: Cell 'AGS of DRXGsII' for '950–1050 °C, 0.01 s−1 (0.2 strain)' is read as 78.62 μm at the supplied resolution; the digit pair could be 78.62 or 78.82 and is therefore only partially certain.
